clips.title: What is Helm in Kubernetes? Helm and Helm Charts explained  | Kubernetes Tutorial 23
clips.why: Nana shows Helm as a templating engine: one set of templates, different values per environment, which is why every values file must be rendered to be checked.
look: A template with placeholders, filled from a values file.
The same chart deployed to several environments with different values.
The rendered result is plain Kubernetes YAML, which a schema can check.
clips.after: Each <env>-values.yaml in our gitops charts is one rendering, so the chart check renders all of them.

clips.title: Misconfiguration Scanning with Trivy -- Ep. 2 Trivy Overview
clips.why: A keyless check for Terraform: trivy config reads the code and reports risky settings before anything is applied.
look: trivy config on a folder of Terraform files, with no cloud access.
How findings are sorted by severity, and how to keep only HIGH and CRITICAL.
Ignoring a finding on purpose, with a reason.
clips.after: Our infrastructure CI runs trivy config the same way, first only reporting, then failing on new HIGH and CRITICAL findings with an owned ignore file.

practice.q: Finish the line so a chart that does not render at all makes the check fail.
practice.after: # without it, a chart that does not render at all looks green
practice.why: With pipefail, helm template's failure fails the pipe. Without it, only kubeconform's exit code counts, and it accepts empty input.

practice.q: Which command validates an OpenTofu module without state and without any cloud credentials?

options.why: A plan compares with the real cloud, so it needs credentials and state.
Skipping the backend means no state and no keys; validate then checks types and references.
That changes real infrastructure, which no CI check of ours may ever do.

practice.q: Put a new check's first weeks in order.
items: The check is added in a mode that reports and does not fail
Its first run lists old problems
Each problem is fixed, or written into the ignore file with an owner and a reason
The check starts failing pull requests on new problems
The check's files join the paths agents may not change
practice.why: A check that blocks on day one makes every pull request red for old problems; one that agents can edit protects nothing.

practice.q: Why does the Argo CD diff preview run on a throw-away kind cluster instead of the real product cluster?

options.text: kind is faster than the real cluster.
options.why: Speed is not the reason. The reason is what the job can touch.

options.text: So the job needs no credentials for the product clusters and cannot sync anything to them.
options.why: The diff is rendered locally and posted as a comment. Nothing ever reaches a real cluster.

options.text: Argo CD cannot run on a real cluster.
options.why: It runs on our internal cluster every day. CI simply must not use it.
